Rules summary Contents 1 SLAMBO! 1.1 Overview 1.2 Setup 1.3 Gameplay 1.3.1 Turn 1.3.2 SLAMBO! 1.3.3 Break 1.3.4 Again 1.4 Win Condition 1.5 3–4 Player Rules 1.6 Special Cards 1.7 Expert Match (1–9) 1.8 Components 1.9 Theme Note 1.10 Credits SLAMBO! Overview SLAMBO! is a fast-paced card game played in rounds called bouts . Players take turns adjusting a shared balance total —but push it too far and your opponent will shout SLAMBO! Setup Players Cards in Deck Starting Hand 2 17 7 3 26 6 4 26 5 Place the start card in the middle with the 0–10 side up Place 1 shame card next to the start card Set remaining shame cards aside as a supply Give each player a player aid Shuffle the number cards (only add special cards with 3+ players) Deal each player a starting hand (see table above) Set leftover cards facedown Choose a random player to go first Gameplay Turn Players take turns playing 1 card face up onto the central pile Only the top card of the pile should be visible The starting balance total is 5 Each time you play a card: Adjust the balance total by the number on the card Blue cards raise the total Red cards lower the total Shout the new total SLAMBO! If the balance total goes:* Above 10 Below 0 👉 Your opponent shouts SLAMBO! and you lose the bout The losing player takes all shame cards from the middle Break If both players run out of cards and no one is SLAMBO’d: The referee calls BREAK! No one takes shame cards Add 1 shame card next to the start card Important: The next bout will be worth more shame Again If no player has 3 shame cards: Play another bout The loser of the last bout goes first If the last bout ended in a break:*The player who went second goes first Win Condition If any player has 3 or more shame cards at the end of a bout:*That player loses The remaining player wins 3–4 Player Rules Shuffle the 6 special cards into the deck The game ends immediately when any player has 3 or more shame That player loses All other players win Special Cards After adjusting the balance total, reverse the turn order If a player has no cards left, skip their turn Special effects: Choose whether a card’s number is positive or negative Copy the last card played**If the last card copied something, copy that result Expert Match (1–9) For a more suspenseful game: Flip the start card to the 1–9 side Now SLAMBO occurs if the balance total goes: Above 9 Below 1 ==Example==*Player 1 plays a blue 4 → “9!” Player 2 plays red -7 → “2!” Later in the bout: Balance is 1 Player 1 plays blue 2 → “3!” Player 2 plays red -5 → “-2!” Player 1 shouts: SLAMBO! Components 1 Start Card (Hakkeyoi, Nokotta!) 9 Shame Cards (Haji!) 17 Number Cards (9 blue, 8 red) 6 Special Cards 4 Player Aids Theme Note Hakkeyoi! (“come on!”) and Nokotta! (“remaining!”) are traditional sumo referee calls used during matches. Credits Design: Ryan “Boulder” Richford Illustration: Sai Beppu Graphic Design: Anca Gavril Development: Breeze Grigas, John Brieger, Brian McKay Rules Editing: Jeff Fraser 3D Artist: Filip Gavril

[Rating: 3/10] This game just plays itself. Perhaps if you wanted to count cards it would be much better? My 9 year old enjoys it and it is great to practice adding and subtracting to 10.

[Rating: 3/10] I feel like Reader Rabbit taught me this game in 2nd grade to help with my addition and subtraction.

[Rating: 3/10] No player agency. No luck mitigation.  No strategy. Keep the number between 1-10 and hope your opponent doesn't have the right card.

[Rating: 4/10] gameplay is very basic.    it's a little more interesting at 2 player.  not sure about the basic game, but in the "expert" game, the starting player couldn't play any of the cards they were dealt, meaning they lost the round instantly. it was funny i guess but this is not something i like to see in a game being sold for real money lol, even if it's only $9

[Rating: 4/10] Felt great when the draws were in your favor, but there are hands that no amount of cleverness will save you from
